name: WonderSwan Color
description: Bandai's colour follow-up to the WonderSwan, released in Japan in December 2000. It played original WonderSwan games and added a colour screen and more memory. Square backed it with games such as remakes of early Final Fantasy titles.

specs.graphics: 224 × 144 colour LCD, 241 colours on screen from 4,096

curiosities: Square released remakes of Final Fantasy I, II and IV on it after its split with Nintendo.
The 2002 SwanCrystal model replaced the screen with a sharper TFT LCD.
It still runs on a single AA battery.
Like the rest of the WonderSwan family, it was sold only in Japan.
story: Bandai added colour to its WonderSwan in December 2000, keeping its battery life and its long shape that could be held upright or sideways.
Square's Final Fantasy remakes and anime licences sold it in Japan, and the SwanCrystal of 2002 improved the screen.
It held a share of the Japanese market against the Game Boy Advance until Bandai stopped making it in 2003.
